He evaded my sword with a shift of his <ruby>body<rt>body handling</rt></ruby>, and evaded it again. Then, in the opening that created, he <ruby>dealt<rt>gave</rt></ruby> a blow to my left wrist.

A joint: thinly protected. My hand had not been severed, but the flesh was deeply cut.

Taking a counterstrike at last was certainly a shock. What was even harder to <ruby>bear<rt>bear</rt></ruby>, however, was his continued evasion. He was not even using his sword to block mine.

I could not even <ruby>make him block<rt>・・・・・</rt></ruby>.

If he blocked, I could force through. The difference in strength between a warrior and an ordinary human was absolute.

It should not have been so difficult to make him do it. Reading and evading a sword’s path like that was impossible unless the difference in ability was enormous.

Which meant—

en.html:
For the first time, he took a <ruby>stance<rt>stance</rt></ruby>.

His sword rose above his right shoulder: a warrior’s orthodox high guard.

If anything, it seemed to create an opening. Unlike his previous lack of stance, this limited the possible paths of his sword. I could read his movement.

The contest had come closer to a simple comparison of strength. In that, an unarmored man was plainly at a disadvantage.

What was his intention?

I had no time to hesitate. An enemy could appear behind me at any moment. Whatever his intention, I had to attack.

I followed him into high guard. As for measuring the moment by his breathing—no. Against this monster of a swordsman, that would be digging my own grave.

Without a thought,

I cut.

　無構と違って太刀筋はある程度限定される。動きを
読み取ることが可能になっている。

　何も考えず、
　斬り込む。

en.html:
I carried on with the cut. No need to stop my hand: this exchange I could win.

In simple force, the gap between warrior and unarmored man is <ruby>absolute<rt>・・</rt></ruby>. However exquisite his sword, it could not knock aside a warrior's stroke and change its path.

I had no wish to kill him, so I held back some force. But it came to the same thing.

At most, we would strike each other. The damage to the other would certainly be greater—
